conflicts.description: The Lamp Guild and House Veyra each seek to place their own people among the Bell Wardens, hoping to control the city's air and so its politics.
conflicts.name: The Contest for the Bells

conflicts.description: House Veyra is deeply in debt to the Lamp Guild, and the Guild is threatening to cut off light to the Terraces unless the nobles surrender their oaths.
conflicts.name: Light and Debt

description: Far beneath the surface, at the bottom of a lightless trench, lies a colossal drowned cathedral whose vaulted halls have been sealed against the sea and converted into a living city. Merchants, nobles, and clergy-turned-bureaucrats scheme for control of the scarce resources that sustain it: breathable air, lamp-oil rendered from deep-sea leviathans, and the favor of the sunken cathedral's bell-keepers. The genre is dark fantasy for adult readers, and the tone is mysterious. Every alliance hides a debt, every hymn hides a ledger, and the cathedral itself seems to listen. Rumors say the cathedral was not built by human hands, and that it was drowned on purpose.

factions.description: A merchant consortium that monopolizes leviathan-oil lighting and sells its light by the hour.
factions.name: The Lamp Guild

factions.description: An old noble house that claims descent from the cathedral's original congregation and rules the Choir Terraces by tradition.
factions.name: House Veyra

factions.description: A secretive order that tends the bells and controls air and pressure doors. They answer to no court.
factions.name: The Bell Wardens

history.description: The cathedral sank into the trench in a single night, carrying its congregation with it.
history.name: The Drowning

history.description: Survivors sealed the nave against the sea and discovered the bells could pump air.
history.name: The First Sealing

history.description: House Veyra and allied families carved the choir balconies into noble holdings and wrote the first laws of oath and debt.
history.name: The Terrace Charter

history.description: The Lamp Guild bought out rival chandlers and secured exclusive rights to leviathan oil.
history.name: The Oil Monopoly

history.description: One bell failed to ring for an hour, and a district suffocated. The Wardens blamed sabotage and no culprit was ever named.
history.name: The Night of the Silent Bell

locations.description: The central hall of the drowned cathedral, now a vast market lit by bioluminescent lamps. Merchant guilds hold stalls between the toppled pews and the carved ribs of the roof.
locations.name: The Vaulted Nave

locations.description: Tiered balconies once reserved for singers, now the ornate residences of the noble houses. Their acoustics carry whispers across the whole city, so nobles speak through tapping codes and written notes.
locations.name: The Choir Terraces

locations.description: A flooded undercroft beneath the cathedral's altar where the great bells hang in the dark. The bells regulate the air-pumps and the pressure doors, and the crypt is guarded and rarely visited.
locations.name: The Bell Crypt

name: The Drowned Nave

rules.statement: Breathable air is circulated only when the great bells are rung in sequence, so whoever controls the bells controls the city's survival.
Pressure doors between districts must be sealed within minutes of a breach, and doors cannot be reopened until pressure equalizes.
Debts are sworn before the cathedral's altar, and an oath-breaker is cast out through the outer doors into the trench.
The cathedral's stone seems to listen and, rarely, answer, and lies spoken within the Bell Crypt are said to cause the bells to ring out of turn.
